# no-missing-space-atx

- ID: `MD018`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `headings`, `atx`, `spaces`

A space follows the \# marks that open a heading at the start of a line.

## Why

Without the space, a line such as \#Heading renders as a paragraph.

## Options

This rule has no options.

## Fix

The fix inserts a space after the \# marks. gomdlint reports the line without a
fix when the document may link to heading anchors, because a new heading adds an
anchor. It also reports a line that starts with seven or more \# marks without a
fix, because a space cannot make it a heading. gomdlint may report a finding
without a fix when the fix would change a line with one character in brackets,
such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a blank line, because it
could add or remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

##Install

Run the installer.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:1 No space after hash on ATX style heading
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install

Run the installer.
```

## Configure

Under `rules`, `no-missing-space-atx: false` turns the rule off and
`no-missing-space-atx: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-missing-space-atx` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-missing-space-atx -->
```
